chapter: King Oliver, own trio and Kirby
title: Learning to read; the drummer's job
summary: He learned to read drum parts about a year after joining Oliver; a drummer must keep good time and make the band happy; his showmanship now.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Let's do a kind of summation up to this point. You had been playing drums for this long time, and you had certainly been improving as a drummer. Did you learn reading? Did you get involved in reading?

No, I didn't know too much about reading when I came to New York. I went to school about a year, and learned to read. I had to do a little light spelling when I was with King Oliver, and I learned to read about a year later -- read the drum parts, you know.
I guess my brain worked so fast, a lot of stuff as a drummer... I said to myself...I put it on... The kind
of stuff I used to play, I'm still playing it now, they don't put it on the... They don't write it, because it's too complicated, like... You know, it's fast.
So the drummer was left pretty much to use his own intelligence.
You'd use your own smarts and...

During that time, the drummer's got to have a good beat and keep time. Good beat and keep time, keep tempo. Don't get fast and don't get slow. And make the band feel happy. That's what the drummer's supposed to do.

Of course, now I'm doing something of everything. I'm singing, throwing sticks up in the air, use four or five or six at the same time. And a thing I do like "Tiger Rag" called "The Tiger Rag Snare." I blow through the snare, sound like a tiger, you know. Any time a drummer stays on one job five or six years, he must be doing something.
